_comment: Every robot detector Tengen has had, numbered. Facts here come from each checkpoint's own training record (train_args, train_metrics) or a saved run; nothing is filled in from memory. Held-out scores are generated into scores/<id>.json by `python -m tools.models evaluate` and must not be edited by hand. Weights live in data/ and are never committed.

yardstick.description: 400 frames of real 2026 broadcast footage across venues, never trained on. Counts robots found per frame; six play a match, and stacked two-view broadcasts show them twice, so six is a floor.
yardstick.headline: full_share

models.name: robot-v1
models.dataset: frc-robots-merged: 2,429 human-labelled images from two CC BY 4.0 Roboflow datasets, splits rebuilt by source image
models.notes: The first detector. Its val split is not v2's or v3's, so these numbers do not compare across versions; the held-out score does.

models.name: robot-v2
models.dataset: frc-robots-v2: the merged set plus 1,017 machine-labelled 2026 match frames (detector corroborated by temporal persistence); 3,446 images
models.notes: Trained on the AMD RX 7800 XT through ROCm in WSL. Nearly blind to the lower panel of stacked broadcasts.

models.name: robot-v3 (640 export)
models.dataset: robot-yolo11n-reviewed-aug: over 1,000 images reviewed by hand in Robert's labeller, with augmentation
models.notes: The same weights as v3, exported for 640 px input. Posted in #model-training on 2026-09-06.

models.name: robot-v3
models.dataset: robot-yolo11n-reviewed-aug: over 1,000 images reviewed by hand in Robert's labeller, with augmentation

pipeline.notes: With the identity fix in fe374d1; before it, 0.25 and 0.35. This measures the whole tracking pipeline, not the detector alone.

models.notes: Trained at 640 px, exported for 960 px input, which scores better on held-out footage. In use by the desktop app and the analyzer.
